subject: POC / Trial: Model selection and success criteria

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: POC / Trial: Model selection and success criteria

Hi Anika / Raj —

Thanks for the great conversation today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary:
- Goal: 2-week POC to validate intent extraction, response generation quality, and latency/cost targets for your support workflows.
- Primary use cases: triage + draft responses for English + Spanish + French tickets; fallback routing to human when model confidence is low.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm / adjust):
1) Intent classification accuracy >= 92% on your labeled holdout set
2) Response relevance score (internal rubric) >= 4/5 on sampled tickets
3) Average 95th-percentile token latency < 200ms in our hosted trial environment
4) Cost target: <= $0.0025 per generated reply (token-based estimate)
5) Safe-handling: no PII leakage in model outputs; pass security questionnaire items we discussed

Suggested model plan for trial:
- Primary: Llama 2 13B (quantized) — good balance of quality and footprint for instruction-following in multiple languages
- Fallback: Mistral 7B Instruct — faster and cheaper for lower-cost routing when high-confidence is not required

Attachments: poc-plan.xlsx (POC timeline, ownership, eval plan)

Proposed timeline:
- Confirm criteria & data sample: by Oct 16
- Model & env setup: Oct 17–19
- Kickoff + run: Oct 20–Nov 2 (2-week evaluation window)
- Review + next steps: Nov 3

Owners:
- Redwood: Ben Carter (sales, POC lead), Marissa Cole (solutions & evaluation)
- Globex: Anika Shah (product owner), Raj Patel (engineering lead)

Next steps:
- Can you confirm the success criteria above and share a representative sample (200–500 tickets) and the completed security questionnaire?
- I'll upload the detailed POC plan (poc-plan.xlsx) and HubSpot deal link.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Ben Carter

Hi Ben / Marissa —

Thanks for the recap — that matches my notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

Success criteria tweaks:
- Intent classification: can we target 95% for our top 6 intents (these are most critical)? Otherwise 92% overall is fine as a baseline.
- Latency: 200ms 95th sounds reasonable for hosted; if we need lower we can discuss Dedicated pools later.
- Cost: the target looks fine as a cap, but we’ll also track cost per resolved ticket.

Model selection / multilingual:
- Multilingual support is important: English (primary), Spanish (~25% traffic), French (~10%). Please include evaluation slices for Spanish and French.
- Curious if Llama 2 13B will need instruction-tuning for Spanish/French — can you comment on that and whether we should consider an alternative primary model?

Security / data:
- I attached the security questionnaire (security-questionnaire.pdf). Raj will follow up on the dataset samples; we can provide a redacted set first.

Next steps from us:
- I’ll confirm the dataset sample availability by Oct 15.
- We’d like a short doc describing why you picked the primary + fallback models (bullet points) so our engineering team can sign off.

Thanks — Anika
Anika Shah
Head of Product, Globex Corp
anika@globex.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: POC / Trial: Model selection and success criteria

Hi Anika / Raj —

Thanks — quick note on model choices and multilingual considerations to help your eng team sign off: 

Model recommendations (short rationale):
- Primary: Llama 2 13B (quantized)\n  - Pros: strong instruction-following, good multilingual base performance, mature community support and tooling for quantization which helps meet latency/cost targets.\n  - Cons: may need light instruction-tuning and prompt engineering for best Spanish/French performance. We plan to evaluate zero-shot and one-shot prompt templates first, then apply a small (few-shot) instruction-tuning pass if needed.
\n- Fallback: Mistral 7B Instruct\n  - Pros: faster per-token inference and lower cost; useful as a cheaper route for lower-confidence / non-critical responses.\n  - Cons: slightly lower absolute quality on nuanced generation tasks.

Evaluation plan (how we’ll validate multilingual & quality):
1) Holdout labeled set split by language: English (n=300), Spanish (n=100), French (n=60) — evaluate intent accuracy and response relevance.
2) Human evaluation rubric for relevance and safety: 200 sampled responses across languages.
3) Latency & cost profiling: run representative traffic at the expected QPS and capture p95 latency and per-ticket cost.

Ownership & delivery:
- Redwood: set up models, run experiments, provide evaluation report + sample outputs (Ben / Marissa)
- Globex: provide redacted sample tickets and labeled intents (Anika / Raj)

Timeline (confirmed):
- Data sample due: Oct 15
- Env & model setup: Oct 17–19
- Run window: Oct 20–Nov 2
- Results deck: by Nov 4

I’ll also put together a short one-page justification doc for your engineering sign-off and share it in the Drive link.

Ben
